notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch (tier 1) worked throughout, no WAF/bot-block, matching prior pass notes. Checked: (1) full hamburger mega-menu nav tree, parsed from homepage ng-state JSON (FabHamBurgerComponent.navigationNode) - top-level siblings are All in New Arrivals, Women, Men, Kids, Home & Living, Furniture, Food, Sale, Shop By Brand - no Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Popular/Most Popular/Customer Favourites/Trending node anywhere in the tree (dumped full JSON and grepped). (2) sitemap-category.xml (720KB, ~1500+ URLs) grepped case-insensitively for bestsel|best-sel|top-sell|popular|trending|favourite|favorite - zero matches (only 'sale-' and 'new-' prefixed per-category URLs exist, which are Sale/New Arrivals concepts, not Bestsellers). (3) Site search via the OCC product-search API (apisap.fabindia.com/occ/v2/fabindiab2c/products/search) with queries 'bestseller','best seller','bestsellers','top selling','popular','trending','customer favourite' - 'bestseller'/'best seller'/'bestsellers' all returned the identical totalResults=1247, and 'top selling' returned the same totalResults=433 as the single token 'top' alone, proving the search engine is doing generic token fallback matching (not recognizing these as meaningful terms) rather than surfacing a real bestseller listing - confirmed with a nonsense query returning 0 and real terms like 'shirt'/'cushion' returning distinct plausible counts, so this is not a flat-default-result false positive, it is token-fallback noise specific to unmatched terms. 'popular' and 'trending' returned 0. (4) Direct URL guesses (/best-sellers, /bestsellers, /best-selling, /top-sellers, /popular, /customer-favorites, /customer-favourites, /shop/best-sellers, /shop/bestsellers, /shop/popular) all returned HTTP 404. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers-type merchandising PLP exists on fabindia.com, for Home/Decor or otherwise. Scope note: Fabindia is primarily apparel (Women/Men/Kids ethnic+western wear) plus a Home & Living + Furniture range; this absence finding applies site-wide so the apparel-vs-decor scoping question never arose.
